segments.title: Chương 11: 0011【Anh Trương Vỹ, em tìm thấy anh rồi】
segments.content:
The last class of the morning.

Political Ideology.

The teacher, Gao Zhan, sat on the platform with a cigarette dangling from his lips, completely oblivious that the bell to dismiss class had already rung, shamelessly dragging on the lesson to brag:

"...So, this is a matter of character. The quality of China's citizens still needs to be improved. When I attended the county people's congress this year, I proposed installing streetlights on Yinxing Road. And what was the result?"

"Less than half a year after the streetlights were installed, the electrical wires were stolen and sold for scrap! It's pitch black, making accidents very likely. Just as I predicted, someone was hit and killed by a truck last night. It was a cyclist who shot out from an alley, and the truck ran over his head, which exploded on the spot..."

"Now look at the character of Americans. No matter how long the streetlights are there, no one will steal the wires. America has a credit score system, and people use credit cards. Once you violate social rules and regulations, you get points deducted from your credit score, and you can't get any money from your credit card..."

The entire class listened attentively, with looks of yearning on many of their faces.

A beacon of hope!

Chen Guiliang had been holding back laughter the whole time.

In this era, stereotypes were just like that: everything in China was bad, while even a pile of crap from abroad smelled sweet.

But he had to admit, China at this time indeed had countless flaws.

Those various wonderful descriptions of foreign countries, ironically, turned into public opinion that spurred the Chinese people to constantly improve.

Until one day, the situation began to reverse.

Unwittingly, Gao Zhan had dragged on the class for seven or eight minutes, and he wasn't even teaching any proper knowledge, just bullshitting the entire time.

After finishing another cigarette, Gao Zhan finally said, "Class dismissed!"

As if a starting gun had fired at a track meet, a crowd of students scrambled to rush out of the classroom.

If they didn't run fast, only scraps would be left in the cafeteria.

Chen Guiliang stood up slowly and said to Bian Guanyue, "I asked for you during the break. There are three bicycle shops next to each other over on Chongwen Street."

"Thank you," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang didn't take the initiative to offer to go with her to buy the bike.

Because with Bian Guanyue's personality, she would refuse a hundred percent of the time and would also think Chen Guiliang was being nosy.

Chen Guiliang just gave a serious reminder, "If you plan to ride your bike to and from school, you'd better go with a classmate. Especially after evening self-study, it's very dangerous for a girl to ride home alone."

Zheng Feng appeared out of nowhere, "The most dangerous part of the ride from school to Houjie is the stretch from the neighboring No. 7 Middle School to West Lake. There are a lot of internet cafes, pool halls, and roller-skating rinks around there, and a long section of streetlights is broken. There are often delinquent students from No. 7 Middle School, as well as hooligans from society, wandering around those places late at night."

This was a very serious problem.

Public safety in the early 2000s was only slightly better than in the 90s.

In Chen Guiliang's memory, a murder would happen next year on the street of internet cafes near the school.

A laid-off female worker, retrained and re-employed, was riding her bicycle home at night when she was stopped and robbed by a few thugs. The woman only had a little over ten yuan with her. The thugs thought it was too little and got angry, so they stabbed her to vent their frustration.

They hit the femoral artery in her thigh, and she bled to death!

Bian Guanyue thought for a moment, a little scared, "Then I'll just take the bus."

Zheng Feng quickly said, "Classmate Bian, I can protect you. We can ride home together, and we can ask a few other boys to join us. With more people, the thugs won't dare to cause trouble."

"No need. Thank you for the kind offer," Bian Guanyue said.

Zheng Feng was surprisingly happy despite being rejected, because Bian Guanyue had said six words to him.

Not only was the word count of their conversation increasing, but it also included a "thank you."

Li Jun, who was listening to their conversation from the side, said disdainfully, "What's there to be afraid of? My uncle is in the police. Next time you run into thugs, just mention my uncle's name, and I guarantee they'll run away as fast as they can!"

Bian Guanyue didn't reply, silently picking up her schoolbag and leaving.

The county town wasn't large, so day students usually went home for lunch.

Of course, the situation would change in the second semester of senior year. During the final push for the gaokao, lunch break was only half an hour, including the time spent queuing for food.

Zheng Feng hurried to catch up, following behind Bian Guanyue like a devoted admirer.

Xie Yang appeared at some point, staring at Zheng Feng's back with contempt, "What a fucking follower."

Chen Guiliang chuckled.

Because he knew that the more Zheng Feng followed her like this, the more annoyed Bian Guanyue would become.

Li Jun grabbed his schoolbag and left. Having been ignored by Bian Guanyue multiple times, he was already a bit disheartened. This guy planned to switch to a new target; Ou Yafei from the next class was a good option, as he heard she had just broken up with her boyfriend.

Chen Guiliang and Xie Yang went to the cafeteria together. Halfway there, the school broadcast suddenly started.

A junior schoolmate, with a sweet announcer's voice, delivered an empty yet ornate opening, quickly getting to the point, "Tao Xue from Class 10 of Grade 10 has requested Jay Chou's 'Coward' for Zhang Wei from Class 1 of Grade 12. Her dedication message is: Senior Zhang Wei, you'd better not let me catch you!"

Xie Yang asked doubtfully, "Is there someone named Zhang Wei in Class 1?"

Chen Guiliang smiled, "He might be a transfer student from this year."

The two of them had been in Class 1 before the arts and sciences split, so they were very familiar with the situation there.

The two went to the cafeteria and quickly finished their lunch.

Chen Guiliang neither returned to the classroom nor went to the dormitory for a nap. Instead, he walked towards the school's main gate.

Xie Yang didn't ask what he was up to, just followed with his hands in his pockets.

After leaving the school gate and walking for a few more minutes, Chen Guiliang entered a pharmacy.

Xie Yang finally couldn't help it, "You're buying medicine?"

"Weighing myself."

Chen Guiliang stepped onto the scale, looked at the dial, and said, "I'm already 114.3 jin. The results are better than expected. I'll aim to gain up to 125 jin in a month."

After speaking, Chen Guiliang turned and walked out of the pharmacy, heading straight back to school without doing anything else.

"Damn!"

"What the fuck did I follow him for?"

Xie Yang cursed and hurried to catch up.

As they were heading back to the dorm for their afternoon nap, a girl with short hair was going from classroom to classroom looking for someone.

"Excuse me, do you know a tall and thin guy?"

"What's his name?"

"Zhang Wei. Um... it might be another name. He said he's from Class 1 of Grade 12, but there's no one with that name in Class 1."

"There are a lot of tall and thin guys. I don't know which one you're looking for."

"The one who's really, really skinny. He was selling books at a stall by the newspaper stand a few days ago. He's very well-read in literature and can casually comment on Dream of the Red Chamber. He tricked me into buying a book and said I was welcome to discuss literature with him anytime, but the name he gave was fake."

"I'm not too sure. You should ask someone else."

"Haah!"

Chen Guiliang yawned, stretching as he sat up in bed.

That was a good, long sleep.

Huh, something's not right.

Chen Guiliang felt what was happening down below and was speechless.

It was just an afternoon nap, but he woke up with a boner.

Youth!

"What time is it?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Xie Yang was sound asleep, snoring.

Yang Hao from bed number 6 answered, "Class starts in 40 minutes."

Chen Guiliang waited for it to go down before hopping off the top bunk. He noticed a seam in his pants had split and borrowed a sewing kit from Yang Hao.

In this miserable high school life, you even had to mend your own clothes.

Having not done any needlework for twenty years, Chen Guiliang's skills were a bit rusty, and he stitched his pants up crookedly.

I need to get a girlfriend soon, find a girl to mend my pants for me.

Does Bian Guanyue know how to sew?

If not, I'll just have her practice more.

"CLANG CLANG CLANG CLANG!"

After putting on his pants, Chen Guiliang kicked the iron bed frame hard a few times.

Xie Yang was startled awake from his dream, sitting up with a jolt and asking, "Earthquake?"

"Time for class," Chen Guiliang said, turning to walk out of the dorm room.

Xie Yang was so mad he cursed, "You fucking psycho!"

Yang Hao burst out laughing.

Bian Guanyue and Zheng Feng entered the classroom one after another again.

Not like a couple.

More like a rich young lady and her lackey.

Before Bian Guanyue even reached her seat, she saw a short-haired girl at Chen Guiliang's desk.

She didn't think much of it, assuming it was someone from their class.

"Hi!"

Tao Xue proactively waved a greeting.

"Hi," Bian Guanyue responded and sat down.

Tao Xue smiled, "Senior, you're so pretty."

Bian Guanyue said, "Thank you."

Tao Xue then asked, "Senior, you're Chen Guiliang's deskmate. Is he a compulsive liar?"

"Hmm?" Bian Guanyue didn't understand.

Tao Xue said, "He tricked me into buying Dream of the Red Chamber a few days ago and also tricked my dorm mates into buying a lot of magazines. He also said his name was Zhang Wei and that he used to be the president of the literature club. But I asked around, and there's no president of the literature club named Zhang Wei!"

Bian Guanyue's curiosity was piqued, and she asked, "How much money did he cheat you out of?"

"A little over ten yuan," Tao Xue said, then added, "It wasn't really cheating, just tricking us into buying his books. Actually, his books are quite good, and they even have his reading notes annotated in them. I've read them, and the annotations are exceptionally well-written."

"If you weren't cheated out of money, then why are you looking for him?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Tao Xue said excitedly, "He toyed with my emotions! He said he was good friends with Guo Xiaosi and told me to come find him anytime to discuss literature. Turns out his name was fake, and I even wanted to ask him for Guo Xiaosi's QQ number!"

"You can wait, then," Bian Guanyue said, losing interest.

Zheng Feng, who had been eavesdropping from diagonally in front of them, turned his head at this point and said, "He definitely doesn't know Guo Xiaosi."

Tao Xue said indignantly, "Liar!"

As they were talking, Chen Guiliang had already walked over.

He wasn't flustered at the sight of Tao Xue, calmly saying, "Junior, you look very pretty today. Did you get your hair done?"

"You think this hairstyle looks good too?"

Tao Xue had intended to come and confront him, but upon hearing this, she brightened up, "We have the day off today to clear out the classrooms for the Grade 11 exams. I specifically chose this hairstyle when I got my hair done this morning. I heard it's very popular in Korea."

Chen Guiliang praised, "This hairstyle suits you especially well. It's refreshing and has an artistic vibe."

"I think so too!"

With just a few words, Tao Xue was no longer angry. Instead, she thought Chen Guiliang had good taste and started chatting animatedly about interesting things.

Bian Guanyue, who had been engrossed in her book, now looked up at Chen Guiliang, then at the smugly pleased Tao Xue. It felt like watching a little white rabbit encounter a big bad wolf.

She was being led by the nose the entire time.

The topic quickly shifted to literature. Tao Xue said, "Last night I read Wang Xiaobo's 'A Maverick Pig,' and I really related to it. I felt like I was also a pig, but not as brave as Wang Xiaobo's pig."

Chen Guiliang could talk about these things off the cuff, "It's normal for you to relate. Because the core idea of this essay is 'anti-discipline.' The French philosopher Michel Foucault believed that 'discipline' originally referred to the control of prisoners in a prison. He then extended this analogy to institutions like schools and hospitals, arguing that the prison model has infiltrated every corner of modern society. You, being in school now, are one of those being disciplined..."

The more Tao Xue listened, the more amazed she became, "Senior, you know so much!"

Chen Guiliang smiled, "I'm a maverick pig myself. I'm still on probation right now. You can ask around and find out what I've been up to at school these past two years."

Tao Xue said admiringly, "I've already asked around. Senior, your experiences are especially exciting. You even put up a big-character poster on the principal's office door, using stinky, spoiled soup from the cafeteria to paste it up."

"Don't learn from me," Chen Guiliang advised, "When you get a little older, you'll understand that the discipline from school might just be a kind of happiness you'll never experience again."

Tao Xue asked, "Why would it be a kind of happiness?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Because this kind of discipline comes from goodwill, and it's far too gentle. In the future, it will be hard to find such goodwill and gentleness again. People in society will really eat you alive."

Tao Xue didn't quite understand, but that didn't stop her from thinking Chen Guiliang was very impressive.

The two chatted until it was almost time for class. Tao Xue waved a cheerful goodbye, "'Zhang Wei' Senior, I had a great time today. I'll come find you to talk about literature again next time."

Chen Guiliang let out a long sigh of relief, having finally sent the junior schoolmate away.

Literary girls are not to be trifled with; their brains are all a bit screwy.

Chen Guiliang himself was a literary youth; he knew his own kind all too well.

Bian Guanyue suddenly interjected without warning, "Who is Michel Foucault?"

Chen Guiliang said, "A homosexual who died of AIDS, and also a veteran mental patient."

This person was even a member of the French Communist Party for a few years in the 50s.

Bian Guanyue: "..."
